rules.boundary: rule K1: at step 0 and at the first rollout start at or past each multiple of checkpoint_every a checkpoint is saved; then, in every run whether interrupted or not, everything random (python, numpy, torch, the action space and the vec env) is reseeded with 100,000 x seed + 100 x b (b = that multiple / checkpoint_every; env i resets with that + i), every env is reset, the reward normalisation's running returns are zeroed and the model's last observation and episode starts are set from that reset.  A resume loads the newest intact checkpoint without letting the library reset the envs, continues the step count and the schedule, and does the same boundary before its first rollout
rules.checkpoint: a checkpoint is s2load's four files, the record last; its record holds the run state as it is before that step's check (the task weights in force, the fix, the monitor history, the no-gain count, the checks done, any stop, the flags).  Kept locally: each check's and the newest two (rule K2).  When learn() returns, a final checkpoint is saved if the last step has none
rules.resume: rules K4, K5: a resume is refused, in this order, on no run.json; a stopped run; other settings (every argument given must be the run's; the env configs as built today, but for the named freeze and the task names, must be the run's); other inputs (the envs are built from the run's stored configs, which name the freeze the run started on and its tasks: a used file's sha256 or entry hash, the plant's inputs or the resolved task table that differs; a later freeze of the set is accepted when these are unchanged, and both freezes are recorded); other sources than the last session's unless --allow-source-change, or unless an earlier session given it ran on the same sources (SOURCE_ALLOWANCE_RULE); other library versions than the last session's (s2load.comparable) unless --allow-version-change; a checkpoint whose run_uuid or settings hash is not the run's; a fingerprint that is not reproduced within 1e-5.  A checkpoint that fails its integrity check is skipped with its reason.  No intact checkpoint is no refusal: the job restarts from step 0 in place and is the same run.  The run state is taken from the checkpoint's record: run.json's live fields are rebuilt from it (its list of checkpoints holds the step resumed from, whether or not the session that saved it lived to write so), later entries move to the session's discarded_after_resume (the attempts logged for a check on the checkpoint itself are kept), updates.jsonl is cut back to the resumed step, a check that is due at that step and has no record naming that checkpoint is run, and the rules are applied to the records as the uninterrupted run applies them.  A monitor_<n>.json of the resumed step that cannot be read (a copy that was cut short) is no record (rule M1): it is kept beside and the check is run
rules.updates: updates.jsonl holds one line per PPO update: session, update (the run's count), steps (the env steps the policy was trained on after it), minibatch_steps_run (the optimizer steps PPO really made, counted by a wrapper around the optimizer's step: target_kl stops an update without a message, lesson 16) of minibatch_steps_possible, approx_kl, clip_fraction, explained_variance, value_loss, std_mean (the mean of exp(log_std)), lr, ep_len_mean and ep_rew_mean (over the episodes that ended in the update's rollout; the reward before normalisation; null if none ended) and wall_s (the rollout and the update)
rules.kl_cut: rule O3: if the median share of minibatch steps run over a check interval (the updates after the previous check, up to this one) is under one half, run.json carries flags.kl_cut and the lead is told; it stops nothing
rules.rate: gates/rate.json, per session: first_rollout (the session's first rollout: env steps per wall second, no update in it) and first_three (its first three rollouts, two updates included: S2-8's rate), each with the CPU seconds of the trainer and of the workers, the workers, the vCPUs, the resident memory of the trainer and of each worker, and the machine's load.  The clock starts after the session's first boundary, and what the trainer does at later rollout starts (a checkpoint, a check with its monitor child, a boundary) is left out of the wall seconds
rules.gates: gates false (--no-gates): no G8a short form, no R0L baseline and no check, so no G8b, no fix and no stop rule; for validation runs and tests; it is a setting of the run
rules.fine_tune: rule K8: a fine-tune is a new job directory and run id from a parent's checkpoint and statistics (the same layout), the parent's log_std, its own boundaries and checks, and a constant learning rate r: the parent's schedule value p at the parent's step if every minibatch step of each of 6 updates runs at p from the parent's checkpoint, else the largest of 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-5, 3e-6 below p at which they all run; if none does the fine-tune does not run
rules.retry: the lead's ruling of 16 Nov 2026 (the fifth list, 2): after the halt for two attempts at one check that were never closed, the lead has the fault repaired and resumes with a recorded parameter (--retry-check; sessions[].retry_check), which lets that check run once more per resume; the attempt is logged with after_halt
rules.baseline: rule M1: R0L's baseline is made once per run, before its first rollout; run.json baseline holds its record's sha256, its summary and, per episode, the condition, the seed, the outcome and the survival (with the state digest where the record holds one).  A resume reads monitor/r0l.json and refuses one that is not the record run.json names.  If the file is lost, or cannot be read (it is then kept beside as r0l.unreadable.s<k>.json), R0L's episodes are run again and compared with what run.json holds, episode for episode and in the summary: equal, the new record takes the old one's place and the session is named under baseline.remade; not equal, the new record is kept as r0l.differs.s<k>.json, nothing is replaced and the run halts and goes to the lead (the run's checks were read against the lost one)
rules.children: an attempt at a check, or at the baseline, holds its monitor child's pid, that process's start time (clock ticks since boot) and the boot id, written when the child has started.  A resume ends, with SIGKILL, every such child of an earlier session on this host that is still alive under an attempt that was never closed (the trainer was killed alone while its monitor ran), before any check or baseline is run: two monitors never write one record.  The attempt stays what it was, an interruption (rule M1); the session lists what it ended under ended_children.  The trainer waits for its monitor child without a timeout (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026): a timeout would close a hung attempt with an exit code and count it toward the two closed attempts; a hang is ended by whoever watches the run, who kills the job's process group, and the attempt that was never closed is an interruption
rules.filter: rule O4 is measured before any run: a run that is not tiny, and rule O3's probe on any set but the Stage 1 view, is refused when filter.json holds no choice, unless the caller names the filter (config filter_hz); a tiny run then takes the env's own default
rules.source_allowance: the lead's ruling 12 of 17 Nov 2026: an allowance for moved sources holds for the rest of the run for the same sources.  A session given --allow-source-change records the hash of the sources it runs on in run.json sources_allowed (with its index), once per hash; a later session whose sources hash is one of them is allowed as if it had been given the parameter: its resume accepts those sources against the last session's (flagged, as with the parameter) and its monitor children get STAGE2_ALLOW_SOURCE_CHANGE=1 for the policy row (rule K9); the session's source_allowance names the session whose parameter allowed them.  Sources that no session given the parameter ran on are allowed only by the parameter.  A halt for moved sources (the monitor's own sources check, or the row's refusal by rule K9) names --allow-source-change, the parameter that resolves it
rules.expect_baseline: rule M3 (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026): with --expect-baseline PATH, the committed R0L baseline (S2-4: stage2/tb/runs/s2-4/R0L_BASELINE.json, made by the monitor's baseline command without a job), the run's own monitor/r0l.json must equal it episode for episode: the condition, the seed, the outcome, the survival and the state digest (monitor2.baseline_equal), with the digests compared in both in every episode that ran (the lead's ruling 33 of 17 Nov 2026: in every pair of which at least one episode ran, both hold a digest that is a non-empty string; two episodes not run, which hold none, are compared on their outcome and survival; with no episode that ran no digest was compared); it is checked after the baseline is made or read and before the first rollout, at every session, and recorded in run.json baseline_expected.  Not equal: the run halts (exit code 5) and goes to the lead; no step is trained.  A file that is missing, cannot be read or is no baseline record, or one given to a run without the gates, is refused before anything is written.  The file's sha256 is a setting of the run (settings.expect_baseline): a resume must give the same file (rule K4)

monitor.episodes: rule M1: 18 episodes: the bar's conditions walk/nominal, walk/v0.4, turn/q90_left, stop/two_step, nudge/forward, nudge/left of the run's set at mu 0.9, three each, condition i (0-5), repetition r (0-2) on seed 6001 + 3 i + r, at 10 ms, as the bar builds and judges them; once per run the same under R0L@10ms.  A tiny run takes each condition's first seed; on the Stage 1 view (set S1, development) the conditions are the stock walk/nominal and walk/brisk
monitor.outcomes: rule M1: each episode ends read, fell, unread (a policy row's episode that did not fall and that the bar could not read: not succeeding in any reading; reason clock_behind when its mean clock factor is below 1, else unreadable) or error (an infrastructure fault).  A policy row's episode is never run twice: an error there counts as not succeeding, as zero credited survival and as not up.  A condition without a reference is not_run: not succeeding and zero survival for both rows.  R0L's episodes must each end read or fell: a baseline that holds an error is kept beside as a failed attempt and no check is read against it
monitor.survival: rule M3: an episode's credited survival is its survival time (the fall time, or the episode's length) times min(1, reference time covered / (1.05 x survival time)): the survival time itself for a row that does not slow its clock.  A clock that covered at least 1.05 x the survival time, to within 1e-9 of it (float rounding), is credited the survival time itself, so that R0L's S is exactly its plain mean survival (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026).  S is the mean over the episodes; N the number succeeding with the look (reading 1).  Printed beside: the counts in readings 2 and 3, the count succeeding but for A1 with the look bands kept, and the plain mean survival, which decide nothing.  The credit needs the episode's clock times (clock.t_ref_reached, clock.t_ref_planned) and its planned length: a policy row's episode that ended read, fell or unread and came back without them is not credited its survival time (a slowed clock would buy it); its table is no record of the check.  R0L, which has no clock to slow, is then credited its survival time
monitor.gain: rule M3: a check shows a gain when N >= N* + 2 or S >= S* + 1.0 s; N* is the largest N, and S* the largest S, over R0L's episodes and every earlier check of the run, each taken separately (for the first check: R0L's)
monitor.m3b: rule M3b (S2-4's reading alone): when the mean planned length of the episodes less R0L's S is under 1.0 s, a gain is also at least 2 more episodes than R0L succeeding in reading 3 with the look bands kept
monitor.g8b: rule M4: at the check of the multiple 5,000,000: walk/nominal stays up (read or unread: it did not fall and is no error) in at least 2 of its 3 episodes.  Otherwise, once: each training task that the table gives to at least one monitor condition with fewer than 2 of 3 up has its weight doubled, once (walk/nominal: walk_nominal; walk/v0.4, nudge/forward, nudge/left: walk_v0.4; turn/q90_left: turn_q90_left and turn_q90_right; stop/two_step: stop and start_stop); the reward's weights do not change.  At the check of the multiple 10,000,000 the same reading; a second failure stops the run.  Checks are named by their multiple.  A tiny run reads at its first check and at the next; with fewer than 3 episodes of a condition "2 of 3" is ceil(2 n / 3) of n
monitor.stop: rule M5: counting from the check of the multiple 20,000,000, the run stops at the third consecutive check without a gain
monitor.attempts: rule M1 with the lead's rulings of 16 Nov 2026: an attempt at a check is logged in run.json monitor[] before the monitor starts, with the checkpoint's file hashes, and closed with the monitor's exit code when it ends.  A record is a monitor_<n>.json that names the checkpoint's hashes and holds an outcome for every one of its episodes.  After two closed attempts that left no record the check counts as without a gain and as a failed G8b reading, each of its episodes an error.  An attempt that was never closed (the session died while the check ran) is an interruption: the resume runs the check again and it does not count; after two of them at one check the run halts and goes to the lead.  A condition without a reference is held in a record as "not run" (the lead's fifth list of 16 Nov 2026, 1).  A monitor that refuses to run is no attempt and is not one of the two (refusal)
monitor.refusal: rule M1 with the lead's ruling of 16 Nov 2026, 19:01 UTC (the fifth list, 6) and the sixth list of 16 Nov 2026 (3): a monitor that refuses to run is no attempt.  It refuses, before any episode, when its sources are not the ones the trainer hashed (the checkout moved under the run), when the run's run.json is missing, cannot be read or is no JSON object, when the checkpoint is not intact (no record, a record that cannot be read or has the wrong shape: its files, and a layout and a fingerprint object, the rulings of 17 Nov 2026, 12; or a file that is not the one its record names), when the checkpoint is another run's (its run_uuid or settings hash is not the run's), when the row refuses the checkpoint while it is built (s2rows.RowError; s2load.CheckpointError: among them a fingerprint not reproduced at the row's load), and when the set is a look set, or a version of one, whose G9-ref has not passed for the body on its latest freeze (rule X1: lookbar.LookSetRefused, raised before the set is read; the lead's ruling 31 of 17 Nov 2026, 6).  The monitor then leaves with exit code 8 and writes its reason to monitor_<n>.refused.json (the baseline: r0l.refused.json).  The trainer closes the attempt with that exit code, marks it refused with the reason, does not count it toward the two closed attempts after which a check counts as without a gain, and halts with exit code 5: the run goes to the lead, and a resume runs the check again (a resume with --retry-check when the refused attempt was the one that parameter let run; a halt for moved sources, the monitor's own or the row's rule K9, names --allow-source-change, which resolves it)
monitor.sources: the trainer hashes its sources once per session and gives the hash to this process, which refuses to run if its own differs (train2.sources)
